enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
459 AM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 950 PM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

 - Showers and thunderstorms will continue into late tonight. Some of
   these storms will produce heavy rainfall and local flooding, 
   with another round of thunderstorms spreading in from the west 
   later Friday.
 
 - A quiet period looks to arrive in time for Halloween, Saturday.

 - A upper level system will bring more showers and thunderstorms to 
   the area Sunday afternoon into Monday morning.

 - Quieter and drier weather looks to prevail after Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 950 PM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Tropical moisture continues over much of the CWA this evening (00Z 
KEPZ sounding still has 1.01 inches of PW). Expect a few showers 
and thunderstorms to continue overnight. Hi-res models have been 
very inconsistent, but latest HRRR/FV3 show one last batch of 
rain/storms from about the Cont Divide east and drifting east, 
mostly done by around 12Z-14Z...perhaps driven by a short wave 
just south of the NM Bootheel. 

Our next weather system is currently organizing just west of the 
Baja as a strong sub-tropical jet pushes moisture into the area 
Friday. GFS/ECMWF have been pretty consistent, moving the upper 
trough to eastern Arizona Friday afternoon. This will begin 
spreading showers/thunderstorms to the western CWA, with the rain 
spreading east over most of the remainder of the CWA by around 
midnight. PWs still hang around one inch so flooding will still be a 
threat for the last half of Friday. Mid-level winds do pick up as 
the upper jet approaches so storms should move faster. Daytime CAPES 
of up to 500 J/kg along with some shear suggest some strong/severe 
storms possible. Models showing rain should be done late Saturday 
morning/mid-day, just in time for a dry trick-or-treat evening.

Finally, the main upper trough and frontal system will sweep in 
Sunday. Once again, showers/thunderstorms will develop west of 
Deming in the afternoon and rapidly spread east by late 
evening/early Monday morning. This may be more typical Fall, low 
energy, fast moving type showers as very little instability develops 
and strong mid-level winds should speed the showers through. Surface 
cold front sweeps through El Paso early evening and showers should 
end shortly after fropa. A few showers could linger far east to 
around noon Monday. Warm temperatures of Sunday will fall back below 
normal Monday and Tuesday. The good news is a drying trend is in 
store through Thursday, before another possible round of showers 
next Friday. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 457 AM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

VFR conditions will prevail through the majority of the TAF cycle 
across area terminals. However, another convective round later this 
evening into the overnight hours (04-12Z) could result in lower 
ceilings and reduced visibilities. Winds will be light and variable 
through the morning, before shifting southward and increasing to 
around 10 knots this afternoon. Gusts to 25 knots remain possible in 
association with the thunderstorm activity. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 929 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Plentiful moisture over the next several days will keep fire weather 
conditions low as continuous rounds of rain blanket the region. 
Thursday's min RHs will be in the 30s out west and increasing to the 
50s out east before increasing to the at least the 50s area wide on 
Friday (some lowland areas may be in the upper 40s). Min RHs will be 
above 30% across the area through Monday. Ventilation rates will 
fall from Fair on Thursday to Poor on Friday as low-level winds 
subside. Ventilation rates improve over the weekend.

&&
